### GS-1 — small fixes, odd-numbered gaps (new terminal)

```
COMMON RULES - GAP SWEEP (operator 2026-10-21 19:28 PT: "please 200+ gaps is fucking ludicrous"; read first)
- SIZE: hard ceiling 90 minutes. Push after every batch; stop at a pushed boundary (context ~60%, a blocker, or 90 min) and
  write a handoff: 11_MEMORY_HANDOFF/SESSION_HANDOFF_<UTC>_GS<n>.md. Never leave work unpushed.
- Start: CLAUDE.md session-start protocol, brief. Isolated worktree: scripts/new_session_worktree.sh <slug>. Claim with
  scripts/claim_session.sh IMMEDIATELY. Read new commands with `git show origin/main:<path>` (window error W20).
- Who takes what (no shared list; the gap agent is stopped): GS-1 takes OPEN gaps with an ODD number, GS-2 those with an EVEN
  number, and both take only class C (small fixes). GS-3 takes classes P and O at any number. Classes: C = closes with a code or
  doc change plus a test in about 10-20 minutes; P = process one-offs (ID collisions, stray branches, claim overlaps,
  shared-tree drift, register parity, stale docs); O = observations with nothing to fix (a measured fact, arithmetic like
  GG-285, a known source limitation); E = engine data gaps (a missing free source or an unbuilt factor) - nobody touches E.
  A gap that could be C or P is C. Engine gaps stay OPEN.
- NEVER touch a file a Wave 84 block owns (84.1: web_dashboard.py, generate_project_state.py, the dashboard unit, the NBA
  lineup-window capture/installer/cron, the install gate in runtime_registry.py, the three NBA preseason registry entries;
  84.2: qualitative_data/pam/nba/, 12_EXPLORATORY/nba_pam_mass_tier/, SEATS/nba.toml; 84.3: 12_EXPLORATORY/nhl_engine/,
  NHL_ENGINE/, SEATS/nhl.toml, NHL components). A gap whose fix sits there: skip it, one line in your handoff.
- No order, position, fill, stake, kelly_fraction, live-ledger row, live model, runner, registry cell, pre-registration,
  existing cron line or .claude/settings*.json change. A gap that needs one of those is not a sweep item: skip it.
- ALL CODE through a PR with CI read green; batch 3-5 fixes per PR to save CI cycles; each code fix carries a test. Merge only
  your own PRs. Doc-only closures may be pushed docs-only.
- Closing a gap: a real fix, or evidence it is already fixed or moot (commit, file and line, or a box read via the bridge).
  Never close on a guess. RESOLVED / CLOSED-AS-ARTIFACT entries move verbatim to GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG_ARCHIVE.md (never edited
  there). Fetch + rebase right before every push to the gap log; edit only the entries you work.
- After every batch: re-run the gap-log checks (CLAUDE.md Step 3: the OPEN grep, headers = status lines, the id-uniqueness
  script) and append one row to GG_BURNDOWN.md § "Sweep tally": your sweep, OPEN before -> after, ids closed.
- Report back: Status | PRs + CI | OPEN before -> after | ids closed | ids skipped with the reason.
GAP SWEEP GS-1 - SMALL FIXES, ODD-NUMBERED GAPS. Repo: eignacio1/prediction-market-bot.
PURPOSE: PLUMBING - OPEN gaps down by closing class C small fixes for real.
Read every OPEN gap with an odd number (CLAUDE.md Step 3's grep), most severe first, and work the class C ones: check it is
still true on origin/main (and on the box via the bridge if it is about the box), fix it with a test, batch 3-5 per PR, merge on
green, close the entry with the PR as evidence. Already fixed: close it with the evidence. Bigger than 20 minutes or outside the
rules: skip it, one line why. Write the class you gave each gap you read into GG_BURNDOWN.md § "Sweep lists" (one line each) so
the next sweep starts from it. Take as many as fit in 90 minutes.

END OF BLOCK GS-1. If you cannot see this line, the prompt reached you truncated: stop and report it.
```

models/ file; no pre-registration change.

PART A - The core (~45 min)
  src/prediction_market_bot/quant/: pure functions, no I/O.
  - Scoring: Brier, log loss, Brier vs a reference forecast (the market) as a paired difference, Murphy decomposition.
  - Calibration: reliability bins, ECE, calibration slope/intercept.
  - Inference: game-clustered bootstrap (seeded), power and minimum detectable effect for a paired Brier difference,
    Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg across a family of cells, and one pooled test across families and bands clustered by
    game (the operator's accepted item 3).
  - Money: ONE definition of net edge (k007 fee, YES at the ask, NO at 1 - bid) and of fill-priced P&L per contract.
  Each function meets the quant bar: known-answer tests (e.g. BH on a simulated mix of true and null signals recovers the
  expected false-discovery rate; the bootstrap covers a known mean at about its nominal rate).
PART B - Reconcile and score against the market (~40 min)
  1. Re-compute through the core, read-only, the numbers we already report: the 2026-10-22 calibration engine output, the
     forward-test report's (book, sport) figures, distance E2/E3 and D3 (the script counts 1 challenger;
     EXP-041, frozen 2026-10-22 in 05_RESEARCH_EXPERIMENTS/, makes 2 - find why), each held-out file's Brier. A table: old value, core value,
     difference, and the reason for any difference (a bug in either is a finding: register it, do not fix it here).
  2. For each frozen model: held-out Brier against the market's price at the same moment (Kalshi archive where it exists,
     nflverse closes for NFL with the timing caveat GG-1090 measured), paired difference with its interval. Write NEW files
     models/<model>_heldout_vs_market.json. Where no market price history exists, say NONE: that arm's skill weight stays 0.
  3. Apply BH across the 49 registered cells' current state and say how many would survive at a 10% false-discovery rate.
Results: the package + tests, results_W86.md (reconciliation table, market-referenced Brier per model), a handoff.

END OF BLOCK 86.1. If you cannot see this line, the prompt reached you truncated: stop and report it.

positive control, because it exercises every part (a split, two ranks, a cross, a frequency, a market).

PART A - The machine (~50 min)

     rank(entry, against=history, at=same games-played point) -> "n of N" with a stability score (split-half r with CI: trait or
     noise at this sample); cross(offense_split, defense_split, frequency=how often the defense shows that situation vs this
     offense's personnel) -> an expected per-play outcome; market_map(entry) -> the Kalshi families it should move (read the
     inventory in 12_EXPLORATORY/thin_markets/inventory.json). Tests: point-in-time contract with a positive control; rank
     reproduces a hand-computed case; the cross is symmetric where it should be.

     ranks league-wide and against history at the same point in the season; how often each defense shows a light box. Then find
     the actual 2026 matchups where the cross is extreme (a defense strong loaded / weak light vs an offense that wins light but
     gets stuffed) and list them. No team or player is the target; the machine is.

already our weakest pillar. Fills lose (E3) and the demo account is cash-bound (77.1). A thin market whose mispricing we cannot
fill at size is worth nothing. So 78.2 measures fillable depth and fill-time alongside mispricing, and ranks families on both.
Second: free NBA play-by-play from stats.nba.com is often blocked from cloud and Actions IPs. 78.4 starts from the
sportsdataverse releases on GitHub and reports any gap rather than scraping around a block.

**Surface.** **0 running components added.** 78.1 deploys the already-built dashboard change and rewrites the runtime registry,
so no other block may add a cron line, service or workflow this wave. 78.2 and 78.4 run their builds once in-session. A
recurring capture or rebuild is registered next wave, after 78.1 lands. Last surface budget read: GREEN (76.4).

dashboards, the Visual Dashboard builder). **78.2** writes only `12_EXPLORATORY/thin_markets/` and `exp_output/KALSHI_HISTORY/`

`pregame_shadow/silent_arms`. **78.4** writes only new files under `02_ARCHITECTURE_DESIGN/NBA_ENGINE/` and a new NBA data-layer
module. The gap agent skips all of these.

     archive holds anything.

     families: the 2025 NFL season and 2026 to date, and NBA 2025-26 where listed. Respect rate limits; resumable; manifest with
     counts, hashes and coverage gaps. Run it once here. Write a one-paragraph proposal for the recurring capture (next wave).

  3. Efficiency + fillability table per family: median bid-ask, quoted depth near the mid, volume, how often our flat stake
     would fill without moving the price, and how fast the price moves after public news (final injury report, inactives) -
     for game ML vs each thinner family. The point is the ranking, with CIs.
  4. Where F8 is computable (team totals; player props for flagged players' teammates or opponents), measure how much of F8 the
     thinner family's price already holds (77.2's pricing-share method, against that family's own pre-game price, not the
     nflverse close).

     before looking, "thinner edge expected" honoured), judged n, and the fillability floor that has to hold for a result to
     count. It goes to the operator as one line for acceptance; nothing logs against it until he accepts.

PURPOSE: DEPTH D5(b) - each applied NFL factor gets a market-side verdict (0 -> 4: team/QB base, F5/F6 coverage x personnel,
F8 non-QB starters out, and the engine itself), plus the outcome test's power per family. Pillar: DEPTH (methodology).
PERMISSIONS: NEW files only under 12_EXPLORATORY/nfl_engine/market_tests/ (route every write through _fence.safe_out) + tests/.
Read the rest of nfl_engine/, never edit it. No registry, runner, ledger, cron or live-model change. Closing lines are a market
COMPARISON only - never a model input (FACTOR_TAXONOMY GAP-4 / GG-733).
Read first: ADR-0075; 12_EXPLORATORY/nfl_engine/results_stage2.md and results_stage3.md; PLAN.md; FACTOR_TAXONOMY.md (F13, GAP-4);
TENSIONS/nfl.toml.

WHY
Operator, 2026-10-14: "data application is the basic question: cool info, so what? it's a never ending race" - and ADR-0075
defines application as a path from the fact to a price "tested against the market". So far every factor was tested against
OUTCOMES (ΔBrier vs engine v0): team/QB at parity with the frozen models (W73.3), F5/F6 no gain (W75.2), F8 no gain (W76.2),
and venue/weather NO before that (W68.3). 76.2's own market comparison: on 182 games from 2025 the Kalshi moneyline mid beats every
engine arm by about 0.009 Brier, and F8 closes about 0.0016 of that (inside the noise). F8 is 99% information the ratings do not hold and moves a team's mean by 0.45 points
on average (max 3.3), yet scores MATCHES. Two readings need different moves:
  (i) REAL BUT PRICED - the market's line already moves by about the factor's amount: game markets are efficient on it, and
      any edge is TIMING (acting before the market absorbs the information - a band question, ADR-0068) or thinner markets;
  (ii) INVISIBLE TO THE TEST - NFL margin SD ~13 and ~1,600 games cannot detect a shift this size, so "no gain" says nothing.
The operator is owed which one it is before deciding where the next factors go.

PART A - Power, then the closing line (~45 min). FREEZE a plan addendum (market_tests/PLAN.md) before computing anything.
  1. Power: for each family, the minimum detectable ΔBrier at the n each test used, and the probability the outcome test would
     have detected a term of F8's measured size if it were fully real (simulate: inject a known shift of that size into the
     engine's draws, score against simulated outcomes, repeat). State plainly whether "no gain" was informative.
  2. Closing line: regress the closing spread and total (nflverse schedules spread_line / total_line, free) on the engine v0
     price plus each factor's term (point-in-time inputs only; the close is the target, never an input). Coefficient on the
     term ≈ how much of the factor the market prices (1 = fully, 0 = ignores), with CIs. Same for the moneyline via
     home/away_moneyline, de-vigged.
PART B - Timing, and the answer (~40 min)
  3. Where the Kalshi NFL price archive covers 2026 games: does the market price move in the factor's direction after the
     information becomes public (final injury report; inactives ~90 min before kickoff)? Price path before vs after, per game.
     If the archive lacks the coverage, say so and size what is missing.
  4. The answer per factor: REAL-AND-PRICED / REAL-NOT-PRICED / INVISIBLE / NOT REAL, with numbers. Then the "so what": which
     band (T1 days ahead vs T2 same-day vs inactives window) could hold an edge, if any. This answer goes to the operator's open
     question - keep building game-market factors, chase timing, or move the next factors to thinner markets (team totals,
     props). Recommend; do not decide.

  1. List every modelling mechanism the MLB stack actually uses, each with its file and ADR: e.g. empirical-Bayes shrinkage of

## Why this wave is shaped this way

**Coverage is the evidence, and evidence needs rows.** The board survey asks whether *prices* are
miscalibrated. It cannot answer whether *our model* knows something a game-market price doesn't — only a model
evaluated against live prices on real slates can, and right now that question has been asked of exactly one
cell. NFL and NHL are both in season. Every weekend without a shadow row on the core four is evidence that will
never exist.

**Pre-game first is the doctrine and also the fastest path to countable evidence.** Pre-game markets resolve
once per game and are roughly independent across games; in-play rows are serially correlated and inflate n
without inflating information. NHL plays nightly — about 15 games a night across the slate — so its nine cells
accrue evidence faster than anything the project has run.

**47.1 decides how much backtest the two flying blocks get.** If Gate 2 passes, Kalshi's NFL and NHL price
history becomes a validated benchmark and 47.2/47.3 can score their models against last season's market before
a single live row. If it fails, they still fly — scored against climatology offline, and against the live
market as rows accrue — and the board survey waits for forward capture.

**The prediction is written down first, every time.** These books measured tight. A model that only beats
climatology has not beaten anyone; a model that loses to the market at its pre-registered n has *completed* its
cell (RULED_OUT, with a reason and a date), which counts toward coverage exactly as much as a winner does.

## Why this wave is shaped this way

**The board survey stands or falls on whether the history endpoint can stand in for capture we never
did.** If it can, the survey runs on months of history today. If it cannot, every new series needs
forward capture — weeks of waiting and a cron line from you — before anything can be measured. Wave 45's
gate said "not as tested". Wave 46 finds out whether that means "not at all" or "not the way we asked".

**46.1 diagnoses before it retests, and retests only on clean ground.** The diagnosis uses data already
fetched and changes nothing about the failed verdict. A retest happens only if the diagnosis points at a
design mismatch rather than at the data — and then on an archived family nobody has compared, with every
threshold identical to the gate that failed. That is the difference between learning from a failure and
re-cutting until something passes.

**46.2 is independent of 46.1, and that is useful.** EXP-034 checks candles against *live quotes read in
the same session* on non-sports series, with the "latest close at or before t" rule frozen before it saw
data. If it passes while 46.1's original gate failed, that is evidence the original matching rule was the
problem, from a test that was never adjusted.

**46.3 clears the ground the other two stand on.** The shared tree holds the price archive both surveys
read and the queue every terminal reads. A three-day-old lock file is the only thing stopping it syncing.
The three Step 4 anomalies sit on the one pipeline that is actually live.

- **Deliverable 0 in every block: land any un-landed predecessor, and sync.** *This wave only:* 45.3 alone touches the shared main tree, because the uncommitted queue record lives there; 45.1 and 45.2 work from fresh worktrees off origin/main and do not pull in the shared tree.
- **Claim IDs at run time and re-verify after ANY release or retry** (GG-322). 45.1 and 45.2 both claim an EXP id concurrently.
- **A premise written in a block is a claim to verify, not a fact.** Including every number in this file. *Wave 43 disproved one of its own briefs; that is the system working, not a failure.*
- **Never bypass, disable, or work around a permission control.** Record the exact command and the exact refusal text, then hand back. Absolute; no approval in a block overrides it.
- **Pre-register before measuring, pushed as its own commit.** Gates sized before outcomes are seen, never edited after (GG-327).
- **Push after each deliverable.** Verify a fix by importing and calling the real function. **Benchmark the real thing.**
- **A merge is not a deployment, and a deployment is not an activation** (GG-279).

## Why this wave is shaped this way

**Every measurement the project has is about one corner of one venue.** Fourteen MLB/NFL families on
Kalshi, sixty late-season days, twenty-minute snapshots. Inside that corner the answer is now firm. Outside
it, nothing has been measured — and the instrument that produced the answer (B, null, the H surface,
B-at-entry, the placebo, the coherence tests) is family-agnostic. Pointing it at the rest of the venue
costs a capture writer, not a new venue adapter.

**45.1 moves down the efficiency gradient without leaving the venue.** Lower-attention sports carry the
same moneyline / spread / total mechanics the coverage target asks for, in markets the strategy's own
thesis says should be priced worse. NBA is back in scope on the operator's own trigger. Its first act is a
correctness gate: rebuild one MLB family from historical candles and reproduce the archive. If candles
cannot reproduce what we captured ourselves, nothing built on them counts.

**45.2 tests the founding claim, not just the venue.** The project calls itself a calibration engine
whose methodology transfers. Weather is where forecast calibration was invented, and it is the only
market class with a free, public, professionally calibrated probabilistic forecast to hold the market
against — with no model of ours involved. It is a deliberate, operator-approved step outside the sports
coverage target.

**45.3 makes the record safe.** Seven waves of prompts exist only as uncommitted edits in a working
tree that is 140 commits behind. One careless git operation erases them. It also settles a contradiction:
the carry-forward says the dashboard serves the old page; T-602 saw the process restart at 02:25Z with no
one recording why.

## Why this wave is shaped this way

**For the first time the project knows what is actually in its way, and it is not the model.** Four
waves established, in order: the model beats climatology; the model loses to the market; depth does not
rescue the in-play cell; and now — across fourteen families — real calibration gaps exist and the
spread is wider than all of them. `H` is the binding constraint. **Nobody has ever measured `H`
properly.** It was one number taken at one snapshot.

**44.1 attacks that directly, with data already on disk.** If the spread tightens as settlement
approaches, or at particular hours, or differs between the side we want and the side we don't, then the
`E` that killed every family was computed against a cost we would never actually pay. That is a
recompute, not a new model, and it either produces the candidate EXP-031 could not find or it proves
the toll is structural. Both answers are decision-grade.

**44.2 asks the question EXP-031 tripped over without looking at it.** Complementary legs on one game —
2 to 44 per event — must cohere: a game's leg set either forms a consistent book or it does not, and
incoherence is measurable with arithmetic, no forecaster required. This is also the honest entry point
to the big-hitter / parlay arm, which has been blocked since ADR-0053 §2.5 was written and **never
drafted as an ADR**. Thin, correlated, multi-leg markets are where price-making is worst — and this
survey has just shown that the thinnest families carry the largest biases.

**44.3 fixes the thing that will tax every future survey.** EXP-031 discovered the archive holds **no
settlement at all** and had to fetch outcomes from Kalshi's public `result` endpoint. Depth is sampled
too thinly to measure capacity. Both are capture-design defects, and both make every future analysis
more expensive and less conclusive. The same block closes the operator loop: the terminal is landed,
tested and byte-faithful, and the VPS is still serving the old page.

  exhaustive), nested (a threshold ladder, where one leg strictly implies another), or merely related.

  ticker-string heuristic that was never checked against actual market metadata is not verification.

      or to something else? State the vig model you are netting out and where it comes from.
    - MONOTONICITY on nested ladders: a threshold ladder must be monotone. Does it invert anywhere?

## Why this wave is shaped this way

**One market family said no. The project has eight more on disk and has never asked them.** EXP-029 is a
clean, decisive negative about *KXMLBHIT* — a high-liquidity, heavily-traded player-prop market whose
price already encodes exactly the persistence the model found. That tells you almost nothing about
`KXMLBF3`, `KXMLBF5SPREAD`, `KXMLBTEAMTOTAL` or the NFL families. Measuring relative efficiency across
them is pure archive arithmetic: spread, vig, price discreteness, convergence speed, favourite-longshot
bias, depth. **No model, no season, no capital, and the data has been sitting there since August.**

That is also the honest reading of the standing DO NOT: *never recommend against a sport or market
family on one finding*. The corollary is the same rule pointed forward — **do not assume the rest of the
board behaves like the one cell you measured.**

**The second block is your instrument, and it is the one you said catches things.** The live terminal
has been rebuilt — full black, five modules, model-vs-market scatter, evidence class on every row, and
an NFL module that leads with the fact that 87% of that pool is stub-sourced. It is sitting as a file
and the VPS is still serving the old page. Landing it is a complete workstream and it belongs in one
block, with the service restart — and only the restart — gated on your word.

**The third block has a clock.** 42.3 proved the NFL extended capture has **zero production callers and
zero enabled weeks**, and that nflverse is a rolling post-hoc snapshot: pre-kickoff QB, weather and
referee state is obtainable **only by capturing before kickoff**. Every week without one is permanently
gone. The block that found it correctly refused to enable it, because with no schedule to configure

## Why this wave is shaped this way

**Wave 41 answered half the question it was built to answer, and the missing half is a calendar
accident, not a modelling one.** EXP-028 shows a 16-feature pre-game tree beating climatology by
+0.0052 Brier and beating the one-line rule by +0.0036 over 1,414 games. That is the pre-game directive
working: depth at the widest horizon buys measurable skill. But the feature matrix stops on 2026-07-17
and the price archive starts on 2026-08-01, so the one comparison that matters — **model versus the
market** — has zero rows to run on. The block named the fix precisely: extend the matrix over
2026-08-01→09-30 with `generate_mlb_features.py`, join to the archive on real tickers, and run T-583's
`run_gate` unmodified with the frozen model. That is also the first genuinely unseen holdout. **It is
one workstream and it goes in one block.**

**The doctrine's corollary has never been tested and the instrument to test it has been idle since
Wave 37.** C5 measured T4M-PROJ logging 30 fields and consuming 3, at a 60-second cadence that affords
plenty of time to consume more — GG-320, HIGH. ADR-0068 says the remedy for a shallow-and-slow cell is
structure, not speed. 37.1's A/B harness exists precisely to adjudicate a T4 enhancer and has still

## Why this wave is shaped this way

Wave 40 turned three open questions into three decisions, and two of them have clocks on them.

**The season is recoverable but the proof is perishable.** 40.3's case rests on the VPS reflog and
journal. Those roll. Around **2026-10-29** the earliest window loses its citation and the argument for
those rows weakens from evidenced to asserted — and GG-228 forbids asserting it. Copying that record
into the repo is a read-only action that costs almost nothing and cannot be redone later. It goes first.

**The build wave was planned for NFL and 40.2's own arithmetic redirects it.** The arc said Wave 41
builds one pre-game model and scores it. It also assumed the season being played was the place to do
that. ~215 rows against n\* 2,610 says otherwise. Meanwhile MLB has 132,184 rows and 45 columns sitting
on disk, spanning two and a half seasons, needing no live games at all. **So the first deep pre-game
tree gets built where the data already is, and scored on an instrument that already exists** — T-583's
game-clustered paired Δ-Brier harness, built in Wave 37 for precisely this and never yet used in anger.

**And the NFL season stops being wasted without pretending it is evidence.** It cannot reach n\*. It can
still capture. Right now the ingestion layer downloads weather, QB, coach, referee, sacks, QB hits and
penalties and then discards them at an allowlist. Widening that allowlist is a few lines, it is the
literal subject of the pre-game directive, and every week it waits is a week of features not captured.

**What this wave deliberately does not do:** it does not apply the allowlist, accept an ADR, reband a
cell, schedule anything, or wire a new feature into a live model. Those are yours.

|---|---|---|

| **39** | **CLOSED -- ALL THREE LANDED** | **Countable evidence project-wide = 42 rows.** T4M-PROJ 1,694 → 0 (GG-318, GG-319). Atomic ledger write + mandatory `model_identity` landed; burst throughput does **not** hold → **ADR-0067 PROPOSED**. Gap triage: 10 BLOCKING / 111 CARRIED / 6 NOTED. |

---

## Why this wave is shaped this way

Three findings converged in Wave 39 and they all say the same thing.

**One.** The project holds 42 rows of countable evidence, from a model whose own verdict is UNDERPOWERED. Not
because the predicate is harsh — because provenance was never carried. There is nothing to calibrate yet.

**Two.** The write path survives today's rate and fails at burst. So opening more pipes now would be
accruing uncountable rows into a ledger that cannot take the volume. Both halves of "open the board" are
blocked, and neither is blocked on modelling.

**Three — the operator's own doctrine, now written down and now testable.** The T1–T5 taxonomy was always
meant to work the way a quant fund's does: **decision-tree depth is governed by decision horizon.** That
principle *was* in the record — `EXECUTION_BANDS.md` § Design Principle states it almost exactly — but with
three defects that let a misfiled cell run a full season: it licensed stripping on **assumed** speed rather
than measured speed; `CLAUDE.md` stated the complexity gradient **backwards** and contradicted it; and
`ADR-0014` specified what each band computes without ever saying why the bands differ. T4M-PROJ is the
result: a three-scalar binomial on a **60-second polling cycle** — a speed-band tree at a slow-band cadence,
licensed by a latency thesis T-569 measured as NOT SUPPORTED.

The corollary is the actionable part, and it is not "go faster." At 60 seconds there is ample time to
condition on pitcher, park, lineup, score and leverage. **T4's headroom is structure, and the stripping was
inherited rather than chosen.**

So: write the doctrine down properly and test every cell against it (40.1); build the deep tree where the
factors actually exist and evidence actually accrues, which is pre-game (40.2); and settle whether any of
the season's rows can honestly be counted, without manufacturing provenance (40.3).

## Why this wave is shaped this way

Wave 38 answered "is anything accruing" with a number, and the number is the problem: **one hand-run
of one script produced 802 rows in an afternoon, and all 802 are worth nothing as evidence.** That
one fact indicts two layers at once, and this wave is those two layers plus the paperwork debt that
keeps eating the window.

**The system can now produce volume faster than it can either store it or count it honestly.**

- **Storage.** Every position write calls `_save()`, which ends in
  `self._path.write_text(json.dumps(self._state, indent=2))` — a pretty-printed, **non-atomic**,
  full-file rewrite of the whole ledger, from 13 call sites, under `flock`. The repo already uses
  `os.replace` in six scripts; the one file holding the evidence pool does not. At 802 new rows per
  hand-run this is the binding constraint on opening the pipes, and it is a constraint nobody chose.
- **Counting.** `is_clean_for_band()` decides what enters `clean_n`, and it reads exactly one field:
  `logic_epoch`. A STUB row with a valid epoch is clean. `model_identity` is stamped at the open
  boundary — but only `run_t1_nfl_game_market.py` supplies it, and `paper_trader.py` line ~632
  silently defaults every other run path to the literal string `"UNKNOWN"`. So the field that would
  tell the truth exists, is mostly unset, and nothing consults it.

Neither is a calibration question and neither needs a model. They are the two things that must be
true before "run the whole board in shadow and count only what's real" is a sentence with meaning.

**39.3 is here because the window keeps going to the backlog instead of the work.** 108 OPEN, a
console reporting 169 items overdue for retirement, a registration-to-closure rate near 4.6:1. One
triage pass, returned as a proposal, so the next wave reads a list of what actually blocks instead
of re-deriving it.

# 33.1 — THE T4 LATENCY THESIS · DOES THE MARKET ACTUALLY LAG? · STANDARD

```

TIER: STANDARD. This is the most load-bearing untested claim in the project.

T4's entire thesis, stated in CLAUDE.md: "prediction markets are slow to incorporate live in-game
state... the market price lags behind the true updated probability... the market hasn't updated
yet, the bot has." Every T4 band, the 11-sub-band decomposition, and T4M-PROJ's ACTIVE status rest
on it. **It has never been measured.** This block measures it, and needs no bets, no fills, no
settlements and no ledger -- so its result survives whatever 33.2 finds about the ledger.

  h_so_far, ab_so_far, ab_remaining, inning, batting_slot, ba_l10, threshold, game_date
Both the model's probability AND the market's price AND the game state, side by side, per cycle.

state change -- thousands of events. Re-derive that rate on the fresh pull; do not reuse it.

  handling of the two confounds named in D3. Do not relabel any of it afterwards.

  Define a state-change event on a single ticker's time-ordered series (h_so_far increments,
  ab_so_far increments, inning advances -- report these separately, they are not the same event).
  For each event at time T, measure `mip` and `p_t4` at T and at T+1, T+2, T+3, T+4 cycles
  (~60/120/180/240s). Report the mean and distribution of `mip` movement per horizon, split by
  event type and by direction of the model's implied update.
  *** State the resolution limit in the results, prominently: this instrument measures lag at the
  ~60s cadence the bot itself evaluates on. If the market updates in 10 seconds, this test reports
  "already updated by the next sample" -- which is itself decisive, because a lag the bot cannot
  observe at its own cycle rate is a lag the bot cannot trade. Do not present that as a null. ***

DELIVERABLE 3 -- THE SHARP TEST: does our own edge signal predict the market's NEXT MOVE?
  This is the cleanest formulation of the thesis and it requires no outcomes at all.

  should PREDICT the subsequent movement of `mip` from T to T+k. Regress (or bin) forward

   (b) SHARED INFORMATION. `p_t4` and `mip` are both functions of overlapping public state, so
       correlation is expected. The thesis needs `gross_edge` to predict mip's FORWARD move, not
       merely to co-move. Say which one your statistic actually measures.

ONE DELIVERABLE, stated plainly: **establish whether recorded positions represent real trades.**

Two independent HIGH findings now say the ledger misrepresents reality:
  GG-295 -- 42 NFL rows' thresholds were written by an unidentified actor, no commit anywhere in

  GG-297 -- 139 of 140 T4M-PROJ positions marked OPEN (all dated 2026-09-22) are `canceled` /

And T4M-PROJ's 765-row epoch-12 clean cohort is **the only scorable cohort in the project.** Every
calibration figure the project has -- including T-565's reproduced model-vs-market result -- is

  *** State the resolution limit in the results, prominently: this instrument measures lag at the
  ~60s cadence the bot itself evaluates on. If the market updates in 10 seconds, this test reports
  "already updated by the next sample" -- which is itself decisive, because a lag the bot cannot
  observe at its own cycle rate is a lag the bot cannot trade. Do not present that as a null. ***

  This is the cleanest formulation of the thesis and it requires no outcomes at all.

       correlation is expected. The thesis needs `gross_edge` to predict mip's FORWARD move, not
       merely to co-move. Say which one your statistic actually measures.

## THE RETIREMENT MECHANISM — spec (now FIRING as block 33.3)

**The diagnosis, in one line: every artifact in this project has an automated, enforced creation
path and a manual, remembered retirement path.**

`claim_session.sh` reserves IDs atomically with rebase-retry so two sessions cannot collide.
`new_session_worktree.sh` creates isolation by default. Gap registration is mandatory and checked.
Creation is a machine step. **Retirement is a person remembering** — and that worked when the
project was small and navigable. It does not survive 12 departments, 134 gaps, 254 sessions and
2,150 commits. The observed debt is not carelessness; it is the predictable output of an asymmetry.

**Measured retirement debt, 2026-09-22 at `e9a335d`:**

| Department | Debt | Should have been retired by |
|---|---|---|
| `03_DECISIONS` | **23 resolved-class entries still in the live gap log** | the T-420 archive-move, per its own contract |
| `00_ADMIN` | **ADR-0063 and APR-0035 signed in chat, no register row** | the signing session (GG-126 class, 6+ recurrences) |
| git estate | **40 merged branches undeleted, 59 prunable worktrees** | `/session-end` Step 9 |
| git estate | **54 commits stranded across 16 unmerged branches** | each session's own close-out |
| `03_DECISIONS` | **operator console reports 133 open against a real 94** | never — it has no retirement awareness at all |

**The design principle: retirement becomes symmetric with creation — a machine step that runs
whether or not anyone remembers.** Five components, in dependency order:

1. **`scripts/retire_resolved_gaps.py`** — moves every live-log entry whose Status token is
   resolved-class, verbatim, into `GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG_ARCHIVE.md`. Must handle the format drift
   that already exists: bare `RESOLVED`, dated variants (`RESOLVED (2026-09-11)`,
   `RESOLVED 2026-08-28 (T-502)`), `CLOSED-AS-ARTIFACT`, and one entry whose Status value is a
   full paragraph. Idempotent; archive stays append-only and entries never move back.
2. **A parity assertion in `.claude/hooks/governance_scan.sh`** — the live log must contain ZERO
   resolved-class statuses. **This one check would have caught all 23 on day one.** Ship it
   warn-only for one wave, then make it hard-fail.
3. **`generate_operator_console.py` gains a resolved filter and a new Section 0: "Overdue for
   retirement."** Not just gaps — one roll-up across all twelve departments: unarchived resolved
   gaps, merged-but-undeleted branches, prunable worktrees, ADR/APR accepted-without-a-register-row,
   and session claims with no closure row. **This is the CEO dashboard for the company: one number,
   read weekly, that says what should have closed and didn't.**
4. **Extend `sweep_stray_branches.sh`** to also delete merged remote and local branches (`-d`,
   never `-D`) and prune worktrees. It already runs as `/session-end` Step 9, so the cadence exists
   — only the scope is missing.
5. **`check_register_parity.py` gains the reverse direction** — any ADR or APR whose own file
   reads ACCEPTED must have a register row. It currently checks one way only, which is why
   ADR-0063 is invisible to it.

**Deliberately NOT in scope:** changing any gap's status, closing anything, or judging whether work
is finished. This mechanism only moves things that are *already* marked done into where done things
live. Retirement is filing, never adjudication.
